opportunity: foldcallret proves a single-use call output order-safe to fold, but ActionMarkImplied re-tests it in check_implied_cover, whose Merge::inflate_test arm forces it explicit when an operand has another live SSA version of the same HighVariable over the call output's cover. Upstream never reaches that arm with a call output, and the version it collides with is the CPUI_INDIRECT the call itself attaches to a global it reads as an argument, so passing stdin/stdout/errno to a call is enough to block the fold.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-foldcallretphi.xml (pass 1 off = the spill, pass 2 on = the fold, pass 3 on = a global write in the span keeps the spill) + 3 option-parse unit tests + the architecture default assertion
binary: synthetic bytechunk (x86:LE:64:default:gcc) in the stage test
inspiration: angr call-return variable folding (the fold angr performs unconditionally where kuna's second gate declines); foldcallret
root_cause: check_implied_cover's inflate_test arm was written for ordinary expressions and only sees call outputs because of kuna's foldcallret escape. The collision it reports is produced by the call being folded: a call may write any global, so it carries a CPUI_INDIRECT over every global it touches, and that INDIRECT's output is another instance of the argument's own HighVariable, live from the call onwards.
hypothesis_refuted: The E2 report's ceiling hypothesis (ActionMergeRequired runs before ActionMarkExplicit, so a force-merged call output fails num_instances()>1) is not what blocks the named witnesses: every one of them reports ninst=1 at base_explicit. num_instances()>1 does veto 141 other call outputs across the six sweep binaries, but those highs have 2-22 members from speculative datatype merges, not the single trim COPY a relaxation would need, so that ceiling is documented and left standing.

corpus_sweep.corpus: decbench full_run_address_2026-09-11, 24 binaries: x86-64 O2 (coreutils fmt/ls/sort/du, grep, gzip, bzip2, diffutils diff, findutils find, tar), x86-64 O0 (fmt, du, grep, tar), x86-64 O2-noinline (ls, fmt), ARM Cortex-M O2 (betaflight, cleanflight, chibios, crazyflie, nuttx), ARM O0 (betaflight, chibios), ARM O2-noinline (betaflight). The O0 and O2 betaflight images in this corpus are byte-identical, so that pair counts twice.
corpus_sweep.method: kuna decompile-all off vs on, then three metrics in docs/features/foldcallretphi/: evalorder.py (the whole ordered stream of calls and memory touches per function -- needs no statement mapping, so it covers every changed function), foldmove.py (how far each folded call travelled, over the folds it can map uniquely) and callorder.py (call-to-call order). Both evalorder.py and foldmove.py flag the global-write counterexample in analysis.md when it is fed to them, so the metrics are calibrated against the defect class.
corpus_sweep.foldmove: 1270 removed call spills located; 718 mapped to their landing statement -- 711 land on the very next statement, 7 with one intervening statement (a register or constant assignment), and none crosses a call, a memory access or a control-flow boundary. The other 552 (43%) are reported, not hidden: 167 call_text_absent (the ON body carries no line with the call text, because an argument was un-inlined), 112 landing_unmatched, 273 landing_ambiguous (the call text is not unique in the function, so the landing would be a guess). The ambiguous bucket used to be classified by guessing, which produced 65 false hazards in two tar functions whose spill text occurs twice; evalorder.py covers all 552 without needing a mapping.
corpus_sweep.evalorder: 0 functions gain or lose a call anywhere. 9 functions differ in memory-touch count and 40 in event order; all 49 were read by hand (41 distinct functions; the betaflight images repeat) and every one is an adjacent fold, a load hoisted to its own statement immediately before the call, or a decompiler-artifact intermediate store to a global disappearing (dat_x = f(); dat_x ^= 1; -> dat_x = f() ^ 1;, where the binary stores once) -- all the conservative direction.
corpus_sweep.callorder: 13 functions differ, all inside the 49 above: the script orders a multi-clause condition innermost-first, which a fold re-nests; the calls keep their order in every one.
corpus_sweep.errors: no new error records; function counts identical off/on in all 24 binaries

default_on_ablation.why_held_off: `--assert type vN` / `--assert name vN` address a variable by its auto-generated name. Folding `v1 = strcmp(pass,sneaky)` into its `if` removes a declaration and renumbers the rest, so the probe's `type v2 char[16]` retypes a different stack slot (credbuf lands at -0x10 instead of -0x18 and a separate `char v2 [8]` appears). Neither listing is unsound; the directive simply no longer names what the user meant. The flip is therefore a change about --assert ergonomics rather than about this pass, and belongs in its own PR with those directives re-read.

print_point_guard.defect: The first version of the discount fired whenever the call's single use was order-safe, but `call_output_foldable` only guards the span up to that use. When the use op's own output is implied, the expression is printed wherever that implied value is finally consumed -- possibly a later block behind a branch -- and the inflate_test rejection the discount waives was the only thing holding the call in place.
print_point_guard.witness: betaflight_STM32F405.elf (O2, stripped) sub_8051ac4 @0x8051ac4: `sub_80515b4(dat_200181a4)` was emitted after `if (dat_200019cc & 1)`, while the binary calls at 0x8051b00 and first reads 0x200019cc at 0x8051b0e.
print_point_guard.fix: print_point() follows the implied chain from the use op to the statement the folded expression actually lands in, and print_point_is_order_safe() re-runs foldcallret's span guard (same block, strictly after, no CALL/LOAD/STORE/CALLOTHER and no read of an INDIRECT the call writes) over that whole distance.
print_point_guard.verification: An env-gated throwaway build (KUNA_FCRPHI_NOGUARD, reverted) reproduces the hunk exactly; with the guard the function is byte-identical to `--option foldcallretphi off`. The fmt witnesses still fold (`v11 &= sub_3700(stdin,v6);`, `if (sub_41f0(stdin))`).

related_issue: Noelo-Lab/kuna#657 -- the pre-existing default-on foldcallret gap: a heritage-promoted global assignment is a CPUI_COPY, so op_is_barrier lets a call sink past a write to a global the callee reads. Independent of this option (same output with it on or off).

global_write_guard.defect: op_is_barrier tests opcodes (CALL/LOAD/STORE/CALLOTHER), but heritage promotes a write to a fixed global address into a plain CPUI_COPY, so a fold could cross one. With --option foldcallretphi on, `v2 = helper(g); k = 42; ok = v1 & v2;` became `ok = v1 & helper(g);` -- the call evaluated after the write to k that it reads. origin/main and --option foldcallretphi off emit the correct order.
global_write_guard.witness: synthetic x86-64 asm (target/helper/k/g/ok), reproduced verbatim from the round-3 review; compiling both renderings gives ok=1 (off, matching the binary) against ok=42 (on, before the fix)
global_write_guard.fix: op_writes_global_storage declines any op between the call and the print point whose output varnode is persistent; the guard runs over the whole travel distance, which contains foldcallret's call-to-use span, so every fold the discount adds is covered. Marker ops are skipped (an INDIRECT records a write its effect op performs). A frame slot needs no test: for the callee to read one its address has to escape, and an escaped slot is written through a CPUI_STORE, already a barrier -- the stage-test fixture has a frame store in that position and still folds.
global_write_guard.verification: built without the barrier and otherwise identical: the counterexample folds again and stage assertion #5 fails; with it, on == off == origin/main. On the 24-binary sweep the barrier declines nothing (the four corpus declines this round all come from the print-point INDIRECT test), so it costs no folds.
global_write_guard.print_point_indirect_test: op_reads_indirect_output_of is now applied to the statement the expression lands in as well as to the single use op -- with an implied chain longer than one hop those are different ops. It declines 5 folds on the sweep (O0/O2 grep main, O0 grep sub_828e, cleanflight sub_8017f4c, crazyflie sub_8009c74), each one a landing statement that reads a global or a frame slot the call carries an INDIRECT over.
global_write_guard.sibling: Noelo-Lab/kuna#657 -- the same hole through default-on foldcallret alone, fixed separately because it moves default output.
